has_ucycle_length.note: has_ucycle_length r n: some MathComp ucycle of r has exactly n entries; RAW, no length guard: 0 always (empty ucycle), 1 exactly with a loop, 2 exactly with a two-way distinct pair (an edge on a simple graph); agrees with has_cycle_length only under 2 < n.

has_cycle_length.note: has_cycle_length r n: some genuine cycle (seq_cycle, more than two entries) has exactly n entries; impossible for n <= 2.

no_ucycle_length_between.note: no_ucycle_length_between r lo hi: no ucycle has between lo and hi entries, inclusive; RAW: an interval containing 0 always fails, one containing 2 excludes two-way pairs, reversed intervals are vacuous; agrees with the genuine exclusion only under 2 < lo.

no_cycle_length_between.note: no_cycle_length_between r lo hi: no ucycle with more than two entries has between lo and hi entries, inclusive; dual to has_cycle_length over the interval; always holds for hi <= 2.

no_cycle_length.note: no_cycle_length r n: every ucycle with more than two entries has size != n (Boolean disequality); the genuine interval [n, n], and the negation of has_cycle_length r n.

edge_family_support.note: the vertices lying in some member of an arbitrary supplied family, whatever the member's size.

edge_family_rel.note: the raw pair relation [set x; y] \in F; a singleton member relates its vertex to itself (edge_family_rel_singleton); not normalized.

edge_family_connected.note: every two support vertices are connected by edge_family_rel F (MathComp connect).

edge_family_cycle.note: the five conjuncts in order: F \subset E(G), 2 < #|support|, #|F| = #|support|, incidence degree two on the support, connected support; a triangle beside an uncovered vertex qualifies, disjoint triangles and malformed members do not.

edge_family_cycle_count.note: the number of qualifying families; zero on graphs with at most two vertices, one on K_3.

has_edge_family_cycle_length.note: some qualifying family has exactly l support vertices; impossible for l <= 2.
